boards.title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
boards.description: Ten named public destinations on corridors within the University of San Francisco’s practical San Francisco orbit.

cards.title: Rossi’s field-and-court block
cards.subtitle: Arguello Boulevard corridor at Anza Street
cards.notes: Head to the Arguello-and-Anza corner to use the park’s lawns, sport courts, children’s play area, or Rossi Pool facility.
cards.short_summary: A named Arguello corner with multiple outdoor recreation features.
cards.evidence_claim: San Francisco Recreation and Parks locates Angelo J. Rossi Playground at Anza Street and Arguello Boulevard and documents lawns, field sports, play space, pool, and sport courts.
cards.source_title: Rossi Pool — San Francisco Recreation and Parks
cards.access_notes: The city page identifies the corner and facility features; check the posted pool schedule before planning a swim.

cards.title: A lakeside circuit
cards.subtitle: 11th Avenue corridor near Lake Street
cards.notes: Use the lake path for a walk or jog, then choose from the fitness circuit, half-court basketball, tennis courts, or picnic areas.
cards.short_summary: A named park built around a lake and several active-use areas.
cards.evidence_claim: The city lists Mountain Lake Park at 1 11th Avenue and describes its lake, fitness circuit, picnic spots, basketball half-court, and four tennis courts.
cards.source_title: Mountain Lake Park — San Francisco Recreation and Parks
cards.access_notes: City-listed park hours are 5 a.m. to midnight; restroom hours vary by season.

cards.title: A Carnegie-era library stop
cards.subtitle: 9th Avenue corridor at 351 9th Avenue
cards.notes: Bring a reading list or simply browse the branch; its current building opened in 1914 and the renovated building reopened in 2009.
cards.short_summary: A named public library with documented local architectural history.
cards.evidence_claim: San Francisco Public Library lists the Richmond/Senator Milton Marks Branch at 351 9th Avenue and states that the current-location branch opened in 1914 as the city’s first Carnegie-funded library building.
cards.source_title: Richmond Library History — San Francisco Public Library
cards.access_notes: Check the branch page for current service hours before visiting.

cards.title: The Fulton-side park edge
cards.subtitle: Fulton Street corridor beside Golden Gate Park
cards.notes: Enter from the Fulton side and set a simple destination inside the park; the city notes year-round seasonal change across its gardens and lakes.
cards.short_summary: A named public park whose north edge follows Fulton Street.
cards.evidence_claim: San Francisco Recreation and Parks describes Golden Gate Park as a historic landscape with ten lakes and documented seasonal blooms throughout the year.
cards.source_title: Golden Gate Park Blooming Calendar — San Francisco Recreation and Parks
cards.access_notes: Use established park entrances and paths; conditions and programs vary seasonally.

cards.title: A glasshouse detour
cards.subtitle: John F. Kennedy Drive corridor in Golden Gate Park
cards.notes: Plan a greenhouse visit and use the surrounding Conservatory Valley as the approach; the city identifies the building as a tropical-plant botanical garden.
cards.short_summary: A named Golden Gate Park conservatory with documented plant collections.
cards.evidence_claim: San Francisco Recreation and Parks describes the Conservatory of Flowers as a Golden Gate Park botanical garden of rare and unusual tropical plants, housing nearly 2,000 species from more than 50 countries.
cards.source_title: Mayor London Breed Announces Free Year-Round Admission to Gardens of GGP for Low-Income Families — San Francisco Recreation and Parks
cards.access_notes: Admission policies can vary by visitor eligibility; confirm current entry details with the Gardens of Golden Gate Park before visiting.

cards.title: The long Fell Street link
cards.subtitle: Fell Street corridor at Stanyan Street
cards.notes: Walk or bike the length of this narrow park connection, stopping at its basketball courts, playground, outdoor fitness equipment, or trails.
cards.short_summary: A named park corridor connecting directly to Golden Gate Park.
cards.evidence_claim: San Francisco Recreation and Parks describes the Panhandle as a three-quarter-mile-long, one-block-wide park connecting to Golden Gate Park, with walking and biking trails, courts, playground, and restrooms.
cards.source_title: Panhandle — San Francisco Recreation and Parks
cards.access_notes: City-listed park hours are 5 a.m. to midnight; restroom hours vary by season.

cards.title: Track the Stanyan edge
cards.subtitle: Stanyan Street corridor near Kezar Drive
cards.notes: Check the public-use field and eight-lane track, then view the stadium’s freestanding west archway and Frederick Street entry columns.
cards.short_summary: A named stadium with a public-use track and documented architectural features.
cards.evidence_claim: San Francisco Recreation and Parks states that Kezar Stadium has an eight-lane all-weather track, is open for public use, and includes a freestanding west archway and entry columns.
cards.source_title: Kezar Stadium — San Francisco Recreation and Parks
cards.access_notes: The city lists facility hours of 6:30 a.m. to 10 p.m.; rentals and field schedules may affect access.

cards.title: A 1920s gymnasium facade
cards.subtitle: Stanyan Street corridor at 755 Stanyan Street
cards.notes: Pause outside the pavilion to notice its deep roof corbels and tile roof, then check the event calendar for sports or court activity.
cards.short_summary: A named historic gymnasium beside the Stanyan corridor.
cards.evidence_claim: San Francisco Recreation and Parks lists Kezar Pavilion at 755 Stanyan Street and describes its 1926 neo-Romanesque gymnasium, designed for basketball, tennis, and other court games.
cards.source_title: Kezar Pavilion — San Francisco Recreation and Parks
cards.access_notes: The facility hosts events and is available for rentals; consult the city calendar for public programming.

cards.title: Hayes and Steiner viewpoints
cards.subtitle: Hayes Street corridor at Steiner Street
cards.notes: Use the accessible entrance at Hayes and Scott, then follow the walking paths and lawn areas for views toward the Painted Ladies.
cards.short_summary: A named hilltop park at a documented Hayes Street entrance.
cards.evidence_claim: San Francisco Recreation and Parks lists Alamo Square at Hayes and Steiner and identifies its accessible entrance at Hayes and Scott Streets, walking trails, lawns, and views of the Painted Ladies.
cards.source_title: Alamo Square — San Francisco Recreation and Parks
cards.access_notes: City-listed park hours are 5 a.m. to midnight; restroom hours vary by season.

cards.title: Courts near Euclid
cards.subtitle: Euclid Avenue corridor at 251 Euclid Avenue
cards.notes: Choose a first-come basketball court, tennis court, playground, picnic area, or ball diamond; check posted closure notices before heading over.
cards.short_summary: A named recreation block with courts, field, picnic, and play facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: San Francisco Recreation and Parks lists Laurel Hill Playground at 251 Euclid Avenue and documents a baseball diamond, outdoor basketball court, playground, picnic area, restrooms, and community rooms.
cards.source_title: Laurel Hill Playground — San Francisco Recreation and Parks
cards.access_notes: City-listed park hours are 5 a.m. to midnight; verify current notices because court resurfacing closures are posted on the facility page.
